claim: Amy Acton is trying to double your state income tax.
read: At a Youngstown, Ohio, rally on October 12, the president said Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton is trying to double your state income tax. Ohio Department of Taxation figures show the state collected about $11 billion in individual income taxes in fiscal 2025. Acton’s published platform proposes an expanded earned income tax credit and a child tax credit for working families. Her campaign has stated she would not raise the state income tax to fund her proposals. The $21 billion figure cited by opponents rests on broad assumptions that exceed the details of her plans, including treating medical debt relief as an annual cost and assuming universal free childcare she has not proposed. The claim does not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the scale of the projected cost. The missing fact is the absence of any income-tax increase in her platform.

PolitiFact — Trump falsely says Amy Acton wants to double Ohio income taxes

script: Morning Check. At a Youngstown rally the president said Amy Acton is trying to double your state income tax. Ohio tax records show the state collected about eleven billion dollars in individual income taxes last fiscal year. Acton’s published plan calls for an expanded earned-income credit and a child tax credit for working families. Her campaign says she will not raise the income tax rate to pay for it. The twenty-one billion dollar cost figure used by her opponent rests on assumptions that go beyond what she has proposed, including treating one-time medical-debt relief as an annual expense and counting universal free childcare she has not endorsed. The claim does not match the cited record. Verdict: contradicted.
